note: Retrieval probes for scripts/eval.ts, grouped by curriculum and then by
topic, where a topic is a domain as it appears in that curriculum's codes.
Each probe is a line as it would be typeset on a worksheet, not a summary
of a standard. Probing with the standard's own plain-language text would
measure whether the embedding can find a string it was built from, which
is not the question. The question is whether a parent's actual worksheet
line lands on the right standard.
`expect` lists every code a careful human would accept. More than one is
not hedging: 'the area of a rectangle' is genuinely taught under 3.MD.C.7
and revisited under 4.MD.A.3, and a hit on either is a correct retrieval.
Where the corpus has one honest answer, `expect` has one entry.
Two curricula are probed separately, because a problem from one syllabus
landing on the other's standard is a silent failure: the parent is told
what a different country's schools expect and nothing on the screen says
so. The retrieval section reports each curriculum on its own numbers and
measures how often the scope was left.
Common Core, United States. Domains as the codes spell them:
OA, NBT, NF, MD, RP, NS, EE, G. Five probes each.

OA.text: There are 4 baskets with 6 apples in each basket. How many apples altogether?
Sam has 3 packs of 8 stickers. He gives 5 away. How many stickers does he have left?
Is 24 prime or composite? List all the factors of 24.

NBT.text: Work out 3248 x 6 using the standard written method.

NF.text: Shade 3/4 of the rectangle. What does the 4 tell you?
Which is bigger, 3/5 or 2/3? Show how you know.

MD.text: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its area?
Find the perimeter of a rectangle 8 m by 3 m.
Two angles sit together on a straight line. One is 65 degrees. What is the other one?
How many degrees does the hour hand turn between 12 o'clock and 3 o'clock?
A box is 3 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm. How many centimetre cubes fill it?

RP.text: There are 3 cats for every 4 dogs. Write the ratio of cats to dogs.
12 pencils cost 3 dollars. What does one pencil cost?
A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. What is its speed in miles per hour?

NS.text: Find the greatest common factor of 18 and 24.
The temperature is -5 degrees. It rises 8 degrees. What is it now?
Put these in order, smallest first: -3, 2, -7, 0

EE.text: Work out 2 to the power of 5.
Is x = 4 a solution of 2x = 8? Explain.
Write an expression for the cost of n books at 5 dollars each.

G.text: Find the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm.
Find the area of a parallelogram with base 8 m and height 5 m.
A trapezium has parallel sides of 6 cm and 10 cm and a height of 4 cm. Find its area.
Work out the area of a right angled triangle with legs 3 cm and 4 cm.
Split this quadrilateral into two triangles and use that to find its area.

note: England National Curriculum, key stage 2. Domains as the codes spell
them: NPV number and place value, AS addition and subtraction, MD
multiplication and division, F fractions including decimals and
percentages, M measurement, GS geometry properties of shapes, S
statistics, RP ratio and proportion, GP geometry position and
direction, A algebra. Probe counts follow the size of each domain in
the corpus rather than being five across the board.
Written in British classroom wording, because that is what is printed
on the page a parent photographs: pounds not dollars, metres not
meters, 24 hour times, and 'work out' rather than 'solve'.
The mapping from probe to expected code is a reading of the corpus in
seed/standards-england.json, not an external answer key. Where the
corpus teaches the same thing twice, both codes are accepted: long
multiplication is filed under both Y5.MD.3 and Y6.AS.1.

NPV.text: What is the value of the 7 in 4 782?
The temperature is -6 C. It rises by 9 degrees. What is the new temperature?
Put these in order, smallest first: 405 300, 450 030, 45 300.

AS.text: Estimate the answer to 298 + 405, then use the inverse to check it.
A bag holds 1 250 g of flour. 480 g is used on Monday and 365 g on Tuesday. How much is left?
Work out 8 + 2 x 5. Now work out (8 + 2) x 5.
Work out 4 356 divided by 17. Give the remainder as a fraction.

MD.text: Write all the factor pairs of 24.
Work out 346 x 8 using short multiplication.
Is 51 a prime number? Explain how you know.
Work out 2 748 x 36 using long multiplication.

M.text: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. Work out its perimeter.
A film starts at 19:45 and lasts 1 hour 40 minutes. What time does it finish?
Work out the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm.
A cuboid is 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm. What is its volume?

GS.text: Measure this angle with a protractor. Write your answer in degrees.
Two angles sit on a straight line. One of them is 115 degrees. What is the other?
A triangle has angles of 40 degrees and 75 degrees. Work out the third angle.
Draw all the lines of symmetry on this rectangle.
Tick the shapes that have a pair of parallel sides.

S.text: The pictogram shows books read. One book symbol stands for 5 books. How many did Class 3 read?
Use the timetable to work out how long the 09:15 train takes to reach Leeds.

RP.text: A recipe for 4 people uses 200 g of rice. How much rice is needed for 10 people?
Share 45 pounds between Amir and Beth in the ratio 2 : 3.

GP.text: Plot the point (3, 5) on the grid.
Reflect the shape in the mirror line.

A.text: Write the next two terms and describe the rule: 7, 11, 15, 19, ___, ___
Find two pairs of whole numbers where a + b = 10.

localisedNote: The same five questions, written the way a worksheet in each launch
language writes them. The corpus stays English, so a hit here means the
embedding model crossed a language boundary, which is the single fact that
decides whether retrieval works at all outside an English speaking school.
Five rather than forty on purpose: this is a smoke test for collapse, not a
measurement. Full parity per locale belongs with the golden set.
